answers.label: A quieter corner
answers.reply: I can carry two bowls. We will still be at the meal.

asks: Lend a good tool or teach with a spare?

answers.label: Lend the good one
answers.reply: I will show how the grip works before handing it over.

answers.label: Start with a spare
answers.reply: Then a slip will not feel like ruining somebody's favourite.

asks: A thing is crooked but works. Fix it now or leave it a while?

answers.label: Fix it now
answers.reply: Before everybody learns to lean the other way. Sensible.

answers.label: Leave it for now
answers.reply: As long as nobody will get hurt. I can make a note.

asks: What sound makes a place feel lived in?

answers.label: People making food
answers.reply: Chopping from the kitchen. Yes. Somebody expects company.

answers.label: Someone working nearby
answers.reply: A saw in the next room means somebody is staying for the afternoon.

asks: If something lasts for years, does the maker need to be remembered?

answers.label: Remember the maker
answers.reply: I would put a small mark where it would not get in the way.

answers.label: Let the thing be enough
answers.reply: People using it is a kind of memory too.

asks: Walking together: side by side, or one watching the path ahead?

answers.label: Side by side
answers.reply: We can still watch different sides.

answers.label: Watch ahead
answers.reply: Say if my pace pulls away from yours.

asks: Watch my lead foot or the one following it?

answers.label: Lead foot
answers.reply: Tell me if it tells you too much.

answers.label: Following foot
answers.reply: That is where I get careless. Good choice.

asks: Moon-viewing from the platform or from the riverbank?

answers.label: The platform
answers.reply: I will bring something to sit on. The boards get cold.

answers.label: The riverbank
answers.reply: We can watch the reflection as well. Away from the slippery stones.

asks: In practice, call the opening before or after the strike?

answers.label: Before
answers.reply: Then we learn whether the other person can answer it.

answers.label: After
answers.reply: Then we compare what we each thought happened.

asks: Would you mind somebody checking your knot?

answers.label: Please check it
answers.reply: Hold the buckle still. I will show the loose part.

answers.label: Let me show you first
answers.reply: All right. I will watch, rather than reach over your hands.

asks: A friend falls behind on a path. Wait or walk back?

answers.label: Wait where they can see
answers.reply: Then they know the meeting place has not moved.

answers.label: Walk back to them
answers.reply: I will make sure they can hear me coming.

asks: Extra practice: the weak form or something you enjoy?

answers.label: The weak form
answers.reply: A short set. Tired hands hide the correction.

answers.label: Something I enjoy
answers.reply: We can end with it. A good stance is worth keeping too.

asks: Would you rather I warn you quietly or make sure everyone hears?

answers.label: Quietly
answers.reply: If there is time. I will speak louder when there is not.

answers.label: Make sure they hear
answers.reply: Then nobody has to guess whether the warning was meant for them.

asks: Does standing watch count as doing something when nothing happens?

answers.label: That is the work
answers.reply: I hoped you would say that. Quiet can be a result.

answers.label: It can still teach you
answers.reply: The sounds, the feet, who usually comes by. There is a lot to learn.

asks: A promise you can keep easily, or a difficult one you might fail?

answers.label: Keep the small promise
answers.reply: Then the next person has something solid to rely on.

answers.label: Risk the difficult one
answers.reply: Tell them the risk before they depend on it.

asks: A confusing form: ask at the desk or take time to read it?

answers.label: Ask at the desk
answers.reply: Then we must explain without making you feel hurried.

answers.label: Read it first
answers.reply: Take the chair. I shall keep your place in the queue.

asks: A garden path: straight to the gate or round the tree?

answers.label: Straight to the gate
answers.reply: Useful in the rain. We should still leave the roots enough room.

answers.label: Round the tree
answers.reply: Then the turn should have somewhere to rest.

asks: Somebody cannot stand in the queue. Save a place or bring a chair?

answers.label: Save their place
answers.reply: A clear token, so they need not explain the same difficulty twice.

answers.label: Bring a chair
answers.reply: A practical amendment to our procedure.

asks: Explain a seal before the signature or after reading the whole paper?

answers.label: Explain it first
answers.reply: Then the visitor knows what the signature will do.

answers.label: Read the whole paper
answers.reply: Nothing hidden below the part that seems important. Sensible.

asks: A guest says they need nothing. Offer again or leave something nearby?

answers.label: Offer once more
answers.reply: With room for a real refusal. Hospitality should not be an argument.

answers.label: Leave a cup nearby
answers.reply: Quiet provision. I can respect that.

asks: A small rule inconveniences many people. Change it or hear from them first?

answers.label: Change it promptly
answers.reply: Then we must still listen to the people the change affects.

answers.label: Hear from them first
answers.reply: Ask the people least likely to attend the meeting as well.

asks: Meeting notes: every word or the decisions with reasons?

answers.label: Every word
answers.reply: A substantial task. It must remain readable afterwards.

answers.label: Decisions and reasons
answers.reply: Name the disagreement too, or the reason may look easier than it was.

asks: Two neighbours disagree. Hear them together or separately first?

answers.label: Together
answers.reply: A shared room, with enough time that neither must compete for the last sentence.

answers.label: Separately first
answers.reply: Then make clear what will be repeated when we meet again.

asks: A file number is useful. Should a name always go beside it?

answers.label: Yes, for the person
answers.reply: In clear writing, large enough to be the first thing seen.

answers.label: Ask how they wish to be called
answers.reply: A sensible question we too often assume is answered.

asks: In good order: does that mean tidy, or that people can use it?

answers.label: Tidy enough to find things
answers.reply: A useful kind of tidiness, then.

answers.label: People can use it
answers.reply: Even if the desk ends the day untidy. I concede the point.

asks: Better to arrive early or exactly when the bell rings?

answers.label: A little early
answers.reply: Then use the spare moment without disturbing those still working.

answers.label: At the bell
answers.reply: An exact promise. Keep it.

asks: Old script: copy the letters or read the whole line first?

answers.label: Copy the letters
answers.reply: Leave a space for the ones you cannot yet identify.

answers.label: Read the whole line
answers.reply: Context helps. Do not let it invent a missing word.

asks: Carry a spare key or leave one with somebody trusted?

answers.label: Carry a spare
answers.reply: Keep it apart from the first. Two lost keys open nothing.

answers.label: Leave one with someone
answers.reply: Make the arrangement before the door closes.

asks: A note in the margin: useful clue or distraction?

answers.label: A useful clue
answers.reply: It needs an author and a date before it earns your trust.

answers.label: A distraction
answers.reply: Read it after the entry. Distraction may still have a purpose.

asks: A worn inscription: take a rubbing or copy what you can see?

answers.label: Take a rubbing
answers.reply: Ask before touching the surface. Stone can be more fragile than paper.

answers.label: Copy by eye
answers.reply: Mark every uncertainty. An honest gap is preferable to a confident invention.

asks: Ask a difficult question first or begin with what is certain?

answers.label: The difficult question
answers.reply: Do not mistake a quick answer for a complete one.

answers.label: Begin with certainty
answers.reply: Then say plainly where certainty ends.

asks: A record has an error. Cross it out or add a dated correction?

answers.label: Cross it out carefully
answers.reply: Keep the original legible. A correction should not erase its own reason.

answers.label: Add a dated note
answers.reply: State what changed and how you know.

asks: Someone misses an appointment. Wait or send word?

answers.label: Wait a little
answers.reply: Give the waiting an end. Otherwise it becomes neglect of the next person.

answers.label: Send a message
answers.reply: Briefly. Ask whether they are safe before reproaching them.

asks: A borrowed page comes back creased. Mention it or repair it quietly?

answers.label: Mention it kindly
answers.reply: A person cannot learn care from a correction they never hear.

answers.label: Repair it quietly
answers.reply: Then check whether the binding made the damage likely.

asks: Does patience mean waiting, or paying attention while you wait?

answers.label: Waiting without pushing
answers.reply: Sometimes that is a considerable effort.

answers.label: Paying attention
answers.reply: Then you may discover why the answer is taking time.

asks: At a long table, near the food or near the conversation?

answers.label: Near the food
answers.reply: Excellent. You can help pass it to the far end.

answers.label: Near the conversation
answers.reply: Then leave space for somebody who takes longer to begin.

asks: An extra bun: keep it for later or find somebody to share with?

answers.label: Keep it for later
answers.reply: Wrap it properly. Future hunger deserves a little planning.

answers.label: Share it now
answers.reply: Look past the people already holding one.

asks: A meeting runs long. Take a break or finish while everyone is here?

answers.label: Take a break
answers.reply: A hungry committee can turn a doorway into a dispute.

answers.label: Finish the last point
answers.reply: One point, with a real end to it. Not six points wearing one hat.

asks: New dish: follow the recipe or taste as you go?

answers.label: Follow the recipe
answers.reply: Then we will know which part to change next time.

answers.label: Taste as we go
answers.reply: Bring another spoon. An honest second opinion saves a pot.

asks: A new arrival: show the place or let them sit first?

answers.label: Show them around
answers.reply: At their pace. There will be time for every corridor.

answers.label: Let them sit
answers.reply: And a cup within reach. They can ask when they are ready.

asks: A child needs to speak at a big desk. Smaller desk or taller chair?

answers.label: A smaller desk
answers.reply: A good room should not make a visitor feel like a misplaced parcel.

answers.label: A taller chair
answers.reply: Sturdy steps too. Nobody should have to climb authority.

asks: Thank the person who cooked, or the person who brought the meal?

answers.label: The cook
answers.reply: And I shall tell the carrier the praise arrived safely.

answers.label: The carrier
answers.reply: A useful reminder that the food does not walk here itself.

asks: A useful rule nobody understands. Explain it or rewrite it?

answers.label: Explain it clearly
answers.reply: We may discover which part was never useful.

answers.label: Rewrite it simply
answers.reply: Then let the people using it try the new words.

asks: Someone takes a long time to answer. Wait or offer choices?

answers.label: Wait for them
answers.reply: A silence can be somebody gathering courage.

answers.label: Offer some choices
answers.reply: And make clear they may choose something we did not think of.

asks: How do you tell whether you have made enough room for people?

answers.label: Ask who is missing
answers.reply: That question belongs at the start of more meetings.

answers.label: Ask the people who came
answers.reply: And believe the person who says the chair is too far away.

asks: Would you rather see a demonstration or try the shape first?

answers.label: Show me
answers.reply: Watch the thumb. That is where the exercise turns.

answers.label: Let me try
answers.reply: Here is the space. I will catch the chalk if it goes flying.

asks: Window seat or front row?

answers.label: Window seat
answers.reply: Then I will stop standing in your sunlight.

answers.label: Front row
answers.reply: Excellent. You get the first look at my terrible diagrams.

asks: Study snack: something sweet or something filling?

answers.label: Something sweet
answers.reply: Small portion now. Proper meal after the last page.

answers.label: Something filling
answers.reply: A sensible plan for a very long multiplication problem.

asks: Choose your practice partner, or meet somebody new?

answers.label: Choose my partner
answers.reply: All right. Try a different exercise together.

answers.label: Somebody new
answers.reply: Introduce yourselves before you compare techniques.

asks: Should I keep the funny drawing in the lesson?

answers.label: Keep it
answers.reply: Then it has to teach something as well as make you laugh.

answers.label: Make it clearer
answers.reply: Fair. The arrow does seem to be pointing at a potato.

asks: When a problem will not move, what helps?

answers.label: Talk it through
answers.reply: Start with the part you already understand.

answers.label: Try it quietly
answers.reply: I will leave some space and check back after this page.

asks: Red mark, or a note explaining the correction?

answers.label: A clear mark
answers.reply: Then you tell me what you think it means.

answers.label: Write me a note
answers.reply: I can do that. Read it before trying the whole page again.

asks: Would you show a younger pupil an attempt that went wrong?

answers.label: Yes, with the correction
answers.reply: Good. Learning has a middle, and they should see it.

answers.label: Only when I am ready
answers.reply: Fair. It is your page to share.

asks: A class festival stall: a game or a little exhibition?

answers.label: A game
answers.reply: Something a shy visitor can play too.

answers.label: An exhibition
answers.reply: With room for work that is still unfinished.

asks: What makes a lesson a good one for you?

answers.label: I understand one new thing
answers.reply: Tell me which thing. I want to teach it that way again.

answers.label: I feel safe asking
answers.reply: Then I will keep making room for the question.

asks: Ribbon bookmark or a loose paper slip?

answers.label: A ribbon
answers.reply: Less likely to fall into somebody else's chapter.

answers.label: A paper slip
answers.reply: You can write the question on it, if you leave the book itself alone.

asks: Read by a window or under a lamp?

answers.label: By the window
answers.reply: Move before the light reaches the ink. Some colours fade.

answers.label: Under a lamp
answers.reply: A steady light. Keep the flame away from the page edge.

asks: Find a book by its title or by browsing the shelves?

answers.label: Use the title
answers.reply: I can show which part of the catalogue answers that.

answers.label: Browse the shelves
answers.reply: Leave room for a book you did not know to ask for.

asks: A difficult passage: read silently or hear it aloud?

answers.label: Read it quietly
answers.reply: I will wait until you reach the full stop.

answers.label: Read it aloud
answers.reply: A sentence sometimes makes more sense when it has to fit a breath.

asks: A clean new copy or an old one with careful notes?

answers.label: The new copy
answers.reply: Check which edition. New paper does not always mean new knowledge.

answers.label: The annotated one
answers.reply: Ask whose notes they are. A tidy hand can still be mistaken.

asks: Read the ending first or trust the writer to take you there?

answers.label: Read the ending
answers.reply: Then you will notice a different set of clues on the way.

answers.label: Trust the journey
answers.reply: A good reason to leave the page corners alone.

asks: A useful note somebody left in a book. Keep it there or hand it in?

answers.label: Keep it with the page
answers.reply: In a sleeve, perhaps. Loose paper likes to find new homes.

answers.label: Hand it to the desk
answers.reply: Then we can find whether somebody is looking for it.

asks: Would you put a question mark beside something you doubt?

answers.label: On my own notes
answers.reply: Good. A question can be a more precise record than a guess.

answers.label: I would ask someone
answers.reply: Bring the passage. It deserves to be read in its own words.

asks: Recommend a favourite book or one chosen for the reader?

answers.label: My favourite
answers.reply: Tell them why it matters to you. That is part of the gift.

answers.label: Choose for the reader
answers.reply: Ask what they have been wondering about lately.

asks: A book is too difficult today. Put it away or keep trying?

answers.label: Put it away for now
answers.reply: Use a bookmark. The door can stay open without you standing in it.

answers.label: Try a smaller passage
answers.reply: One paragraph is a respectable day's reading.

asks: You forget to drink. A reminder or a cup already filled?

answers.label: Remind me
answers.reply: Before training, and after. Those are appointments now.

answers.label: Leave the filled cup
answers.reply: Visible, and not beside the ink. We have had confusion.

asks: Rest in the quiet room or where you can hear the corridor?

answers.label: The quiet room
answers.reply: I will tell you before anybody comes in.

answers.label: Near the corridor
answers.reply: Then you will know the hospital has not emptied around you.

asks: Do you want the proper word or the plain explanation first?

answers.label: The proper word
answers.reply: Then I explain what it means. No extra credit for memorising a sound.

answers.label: Plain explanation
answers.reply: Good. We can add the name after you understand the thing.

asks: First paper crane: neat folds or finish it without starting over?

answers.label: Neat folds
answers.reply: One crease at a time. The paper will wait.

answers.label: Finish this one
answers.reply: A finished awkward bird teaches where the next fold belongs.

asks: Would you come in early if you thought the problem might be nothing?

answers.label: Come in anyway
answers.reply: That is an entirely respectable reason for a short appointment.

answers.label: Ask what to watch for
answers.reply: I will write it clearly. Come back if any of it changes.

asks: A visitor when you are tired: company or a promise to return?

answers.label: Stay quietly
answers.reply: I can find a chair that does not squeak for attention.

answers.label: Come back later
answers.reply: Name a time. Otherwise later becomes a worrying word.

asks: Keep your own recovery notes or leave the record to me?

answers.label: My own notes
answers.reply: Write what changed, not what you think I want to read.

answers.label: Keep the record for me
answers.reply: I will read it back. You can tell me what I missed.

asks: Food advice you can actually follow, or the ideal plan?

answers.label: What I can follow
answers.reply: Tell me when you eat and what you can carry.

answers.label: Show the ideal too
answers.reply: As a guide. Nobody heals by feeling guilty at a list.

asks: Would you be annoyed if I asked the same question again?

answers.label: Ask if you need to
answers.reply: I will say why I am checking. You deserve that much.

answers.label: Tell me why first
answers.reply: Fair request. Repetition without a reason sounds like disbelief.

asks: If a friend keeps refusing rest, argue or offer to take over?

answers.label: Argue kindly
answers.reply: Specific reasons. Volume is not a treatment.

answers.label: Take over one task
answers.reply: That gives rest somewhere to start.

asks: Road food: lighter pack or a better lunch?

answers.label: Lighter pack
answers.reply: Then I know a stall that wraps the rice without the extra box.

answers.label: Better lunch
answers.reply: Excellent. We can argue about the weight after eating.

asks: A bargain you need today or a finer thing you might need later?

answers.label: What I need today
answers.reply: Good. A cheap future problem still occupies a shelf.

answers.label: Save for the finer thing
answers.reply: Then know where the saving ends. Markets will happily keep moving it.

asks: Rain on the road: wait under cover or keep a steady pace?

answers.label: Wait under cover
answers.reply: Check the roof before praising it. An important detail.

answers.label: Keep moving carefully
answers.reply: Shorten the load straps. Wet wheels dislike surprises.

asks: First circuit of a market: compare prices or talk to the makers?

answers.label: Compare prices
answers.reply: Count the size as well as the number. Tiny cabbages can be very persuasive.

answers.label: Talk to the makers
answers.reply: Ask which part takes the longest. That tells you something a price cannot.

asks: A customer changes their mind. Return the money or offer another item?

answers.label: Return the money
answers.reply: Clean account. A person can come back without needing an excuse.

answers.label: Offer an alternative
answers.reply: Once, without trapping them in a conversation they did not buy.

asks: A cart creaks. Mend it before loading or test it empty?

answers.label: Mend it first
answers.reply: A creak has earned a little attention.

answers.label: Test it empty
answers.reply: Good. Listen while somebody else watches the wheel.

asks: Somebody helps unload. Pay them or return the favour?

answers.label: Pay them fairly
answers.reply: Ask the time it took. I ought to ask more often.

answers.label: Return the favour
answers.reply: Name the day, or the favour can wander off down the road.

asks: Road story: the useful version or the entertaining one?

answers.label: Useful version
answers.reply: Here is the turn where the milestone points at the wrong fork.

answers.label: Entertain me
answers.reply: A fine choice. The cart will be much larger in this telling.

asks: A future shop: put the wares outside or leave a place to sit?

answers.label: Wares outside
answers.reply: A good display should leave enough pavement for the people who will not buy.

answers.label: A place to sit
answers.reply: Customers with time. Dangerous for my entire stock of stories.

asks: A friend wants a discount. Lower the price or explain the cost?

answers.label: Lower it if I can
answers.reply: A gift entered honestly in the account. I can understand that.

answers.label: Explain the cost
answers.reply: Then the friend knows what cannot be made cheaper.

asks: Carry the light end or help me balance the heavy one?

answers.label: The light end
answers.reply: Keep it level. That helps more than you think.

answers.label: Balance the heavy end
answers.reply: On my count. We can set it down at the next stair.

asks: Pause at every landing or make one longer stop?

answers.label: Every landing
answers.reply: Good. We can check the grip while it is still a grip.

answers.label: One longer stop
answers.reply: Tell me before the fingers get tired. Not after.

asks: A sticky door: oil the hinge or find where the wood catches?

answers.label: Oil the hinge first
answers.reply: A little. Too much leaves the next person's sleeve with a job.

answers.label: Find the catching edge
answers.reply: Here. See the rubbed bit? That tells us where it touches.

asks: Delivering during a nap: knock softly or leave a note?

answers.label: A soft knock
answers.reply: Then wait. A sleepy person needs time to find the room.

answers.label: Leave a note
answers.reply: Somewhere they will see it. I can bring the parcel round later.

asks: A wobbly chair: mark it or move it out of the way?

answers.label: Mark it clearly
answers.reply: I will put a cloth across the seat until it is mended.

answers.label: Move it aside
answers.reply: Somewhere a tired person will not mistake it for a spare seat.

asks: Do you mind if I ask for help before the stairs?

answers.label: Ask now
answers.reply: Thank you. I am trying to do that more often.

answers.label: Tell me what needs doing
answers.reply: The corner catches at the turn. I need eyes there.

asks: One thing for an empty room: a shelf or a seat?

answers.label: A shelf
answers.reply: Somewhere a thing can stay when you go outside.

answers.label: A seat
answers.reply: A place to stop carrying yourself about. That is useful.

asks: After carrying something, do you like thanks or a cup of water?

answers.label: Say thanks
answers.reply: I like knowing it arrived where it was wanted.

answers.label: A cup of water
answers.reply: Yes. I forget until someone offers.

asks: If something is heavier than expected, say so or quietly change your grip?

answers.label: Say it
answers.reply: Then the other person knows to move with you.

answers.label: Change the grip first
answers.reply: Small change. Tell me if you need more room.

asks: What makes a room feel ready for somebody?

answers.label: Their things have a place
answers.reply: A hook at the right height. A drawer that opens easily.

answers.label: Someone expects them
answers.reply: Then I can leave the chair turned towards the door.

asks: Counter seat or the little end table?

answers.label: At the counter
answers.reply: Good! You can tell me when I lose track of a pot!

answers.label: End table
answers.reply: A quieter bowl coming up!

asks: Broth first or noodles first?

answers.label: Taste the broth
answers.reply: Careful with the steam! It has opinions!

answers.label: Straight to noodles
answers.reply: Lift a little, not the entire afternoon!

asks: Ask for your usual or let you choose anew?

answers.label: Offer the usual
answers.reply: With permission to change it! I have other ingredients!

answers.label: Ask each visit
answers.reply: A new question for a new appetite!

asks: Split an extra egg or keep it for later?

answers.label: Split it now
answers.reply: A useful knife and a diplomatic hand!

answers.label: Save it properly
answers.reply: Wrapped before the bowl gets cold!

asks: Busy lunch: quick bowl or time to sit?

answers.label: Quick bowl
answers.reply: I can move fast without making you swallow the weather!

answers.label: Time to sit
answers.reply: Good! The chair has been looking underemployed!

asks: Try a little new flavour or keep the favourite?

answers.label: A little new flavour
answers.reply: Beside the usual, so the experiment does not steal lunch!

answers.label: Keep the favourite
answers.reply: A sound order! Familiar can be exactly the point!

asks: Tell me when the bowl was good or simply come back?

answers.label: Say what was good
answers.reply: Then I know what to keep doing!

answers.label: Come back tomorrow
answers.reply: An excellent review with actual feet!

asks: Last free seat: take it or ask who was waiting?

answers.label: Take it if clear
answers.reply: Look once before sitting. That is all the ceremony needed!

answers.label: Ask who was waiting
answers.reply: I will keep the bowl warm while we sort it out!

asks: Carry lunch home or eat while it is hot?

answers.label: Carry it home
answers.reply: Keep it level! The broth would like to arrive with the noodles!

answers.label: Eat it here
answers.reply: A fine arrangement for my entire profession!

asks: A rough day: questions or a bowl without them?

answers.label: Ask one small question
answers.reply: Then I listen while you eat!

answers.label: Just the bowl
answers.reply: Coming up. Words can sit down later!

asks: A stronger opponent, or one you can practise a clean form against?

answers.label: Stronger opponent
answers.reply: Then do not call every correction unfair.

answers.label: Practise the clean form
answers.reply: Make it clean, then. Repeating a flaw is a strange ambition.

asks: One difficult target or several easy ones?

answers.label: One difficult target
answers.reply: You will have to aim instead of celebrating noise.

answers.label: Several easy ones
answers.reply: Then make each throw different. Otherwise you have learned one thing several times.

asks: Want somebody watching your next attempt?

answers.label: Watch me
answers.reply: Then I expect an attempt worth paying attention to.

answers.label: Let me practise first
answers.reply: Fine. Show me the result when you have one.

asks: Start fast or make the opponent move first?

answers.label: Start fast
answers.reply: Commit properly. A half charge is merely falling forward.

answers.label: Make them move
answers.reply: Then have a reason for the step you are waiting for.

asks: Lose narrowly or win without learning anything?

answers.label: Lose narrowly
answers.reply: Then find the narrow part and remove it.

answers.label: Take the win
answers.reply: A win has uses. Do not confuse them with improvement.

asks: Repair a familiar tool or replace it with a better one?

answers.label: Repair the familiar one
answers.reply: Check the repair before trusting the habit.

answers.label: Try the better one
answers.reply: Use it until the weight stops surprising you.

asks: Would you accept a challenge you expect to lose?

answers.label: Yes, to find the gap
answers.reply: Then come ready to describe the gap afterwards.

answers.label: After I prepare
answers.reply: Set a day. Preparation can become an excellent hiding place.

asks: Measure yourself against yesterday, or against the best person here?

answers.label: Against yesterday
answers.reply: Yesterday was not aiming at you. Remember that.

answers.label: Against the best
answers.reply: Then study what the best actually does, rather than the rumour.

asks: A teacher changes the drill halfway through. Ask why or adapt first?

answers.label: Ask why
answers.reply: One clear question. There may be an opponent waiting.

answers.label: Adapt, then ask
answers.reply: Show that you noticed the change before calling it clever.

asks: Is the boring practice still worth doing when nobody is watching?

answers.label: That is when it matters
answers.reply: Then your habits might survive an audience.

answers.label: Sometimes I need a witness
answers.reply: Choose somebody who sees the work, not somebody who cheers automatically.

asks: Break now, or after one clean attempt?

answers.label: Break now
answers.reply: Good. Set the tools down properly.

answers.label: One clean attempt
answers.reply: One. Then we stop, whatever the result.

asks: Heavy pack. What comes out first?

answers.label: Something I can borrow
answers.reply: Ask before relying on another person's spare.

answers.label: Something I do not need
answers.reply: Explain what it was for before you leave it.

asks: Rain coming. Drill inside, or practise getting wet?

answers.label: Inside
answers.reply: Then we work on hands. Clear a little floor.

answers.label: Get wet
answers.reply: Dry clothes waiting first. We are learning, not catching cold.

asks: Want the correction now, or time to find it?

answers.label: Tell me now
answers.reply: Your shoulder moves before your hand.

answers.label: Let me find it
answers.reply: I will watch. Ask when you need the next pair of eyes.

asks: Walking in silence. Comfortable, or awkward?

answers.label: Comfortable
answers.reply: Good. Watch where the path changes.

answers.label: A little awkward
answers.reply: Then say so. We can talk about the path.

asks: A nod, or the whole explanation when something goes right?

answers.label: A nod
answers.reply: You will still get the explanation when it matters.

answers.label: The explanation
answers.reply: Then listen: you recovered before committing the next step.

asks: This offcut. Keep working, or leave the shape alone?

answers.label: Keep working
answers.reply: A little at a time. The blade takes away more than you expect.

answers.label: Leave it alone
answers.reply: Knowing when to stop is useful work.

asks: If I miss a detail, will you interrupt?

answers.label: Straight away
answers.reply: Say what you saw. Briefly.

answers.label: When we are clear
answers.reply: Unless the detail can hurt someone. Then speak.

asks: Company at lunch, or somewhere quiet today?

answers.label: Company
answers.reply: Make space. People arrive when they smell food.

answers.label: Somewhere quiet
answers.reply: Take this path. It reaches a bench before the next turn.

asks: A hard day. What makes it feel finished?

answers.label: Everyone home
answers.reply: Count the people you mean, then go see them.

answers.label: One thing put right
answers.reply: Choose something small enough to finish before sleep.

asks: Rain before noon, or clear until supper?

answers.label: Rain before noon
answers.reply: A cautious forecast. I will put the notebook under my vest.

answers.label: Clear until supper
answers.reply: Then I shall enjoy being wrong in dry clothes.

asks: Speed round or a neat relay handoff?

answers.label: Speed round
answers.reply: A clean handoff still counts as part of being fast.

answers.label: Neat handoff
answers.reply: A victory for everyone who has ever chased a dropped baton.

asks: Small wager or just the challenge?

answers.label: A small wager
answers.reply: Lunch-sized. Nobody owes a week of meals for a wet sandal.

answers.label: Just the challenge
answers.reply: Fine. Pride has an excellent credit system.

asks: Record the near win or only the result?

answers.label: The near win too
answers.reply: The margin has room. An important design feature.

answers.label: Only the result
answers.reply: Merciless bookkeeping. I admire the economy.

asks: Immediate rematch or time to practise?

answers.label: Immediate
answers.reply: Then tell me what you intend to change.

answers.label: Time to practise
answers.reply: Name the afternoon. I know where to find a witness.

asks: A joke before the drill or once the work is done?

answers.label: Before
answers.reply: Then I have to make sure you heard the instruction too.

answers.label: Afterwards
answers.reply: A disciplined audience. The joke will have to improve.

asks: Beat the bell or finish beside the person learning?

answers.label: Beat the bell
answers.reply: Then come back and show which turn saved the step.

answers.label: Finish together
answers.reply: A very inconvenient answer for a wager. A good one for a lesson.

asks: A nickname earned by skill or by a ridiculous mistake?

answers.label: By skill
answers.reply: A useful standard. I shall have to invent fewer examples.

answers.label: By a harmless mistake
answers.reply: Then the owner gets a vote before the name leaves the yard.

asks: Leave room in a notebook for corrections?

answers.label: Plenty of room
answers.reply: An answer from someone expecting to learn. Dangerous habit.

answers.label: Keep a second page
answers.reply: Then tie the pages together before the wind gives an opinion.

asks: Can you tell when I have stopped joking?

answers.label: Your words get shorter
answers.reply: Then you know which part to hear the first time.

answers.label: I check what changed
answers.reply: Good. Watch the people, not just my face.

asks: Sunlit bench or a little shade?

answers.label: The sunlight
answers.reply: We can move when the stone gets too warm.

answers.label: A little shade
answers.reply: There is room beside the roots.

asks: A struggling seedling: more water or check the ground?

answers.label: Try more water
answers.reply: A little, then wait long enough to see what changed.

answers.label: Check the ground
answers.reply: Sometimes the roots need room rather than another cup.

asks: A picture seems wrong. Look away or examine one edge?

answers.label: Look away briefly
answers.reply: Rest can give the eye a truer first look.

answers.label: Examine the edge
answers.reply: A small certain thing can help the whole picture settle.

asks: Talk while walking or let the path keep us company?

answers.label: Talk a little
answers.reply: Tell me the small thing you noticed today.

answers.label: Let the path speak
answers.reply: Then we can point things out without filling every silence.

asks: Trim the branch now or watch another day?

answers.label: Trim it carefully
answers.reply: Then keep the cut small enough for the tree to bear.

answers.label: Watch another day
answers.reply: Make a note of what you are waiting to learn.

asks: Repeat slowly or try a new example?

answers.label: Slow repetition
answers.reply: We can notice where the shape begins to change.

answers.label: A new example
answers.reply: A different picture sometimes frees a tired thought.

asks: Would you rather plant or tend what is growing?

answers.label: Plant something
answers.reply: Choose a place you can return to water.

answers.label: Tend what is there
answers.reply: A useful kindness. The beginning is only one part of growing.

asks: Rest alone or with somebody sitting nearby?

answers.label: Alone for a while
answers.reply: I will tell you when I intend to come back.

answers.label: Somebody nearby
answers.reply: I can bring work that needs no talking.

asks: Change the plan for rain or keep a sheltered version?

answers.label: Change the plan
answers.reply: We can find an afternoon that suits what the day became.

answers.label: A sheltered version
answers.reply: Leave room for the part that cannot be sheltered.

asks: How do you know when waiting has become avoiding?

answers.label: Set a time to return
answers.reply: A gentle boundary can help.

answers.label: Ask someone to notice
answers.reply: Choose somebody who can tell you kindly and clearly.

asks: Why did you pause before answering?

answers.label: I was checking my words
answers.reply: Keep the pause. Make the words useful.

answers.label: I was not sure
answers.reply: A reason to ask, rather than guess.

asks: One precise question or several simple ones?

answers.label: One precise question
answers.reply: Then make sure it contains only one thing.

answers.label: Several simple ones
answers.reply: Leave enough silence for each answer.

asks: Hear the whole account before taking notes?

answers.label: Hear it first
answers.reply: Then write before your memory tidies it.

answers.label: Notes as we go
answers.reply: Look up often enough to notice the person.

asks: Check the surprising detail or the ordinary one?

answers.label: The surprising detail
answers.reply: Ask how it was noticed.

answers.label: The ordinary one
answers.reply: Good. Familiar things are easy to copy without seeing.

asks: Would you rather correct yourself or hear my question?

answers.label: Let me correct it
answers.reply: You have time.

answers.label: Ask the question
answers.reply: What did you see, before deciding what it meant?

asks: Does a silence always need another question?

answers.label: Leave it a moment
answers.reply: A sensible use of a moment.

answers.label: Ask if they need time
answers.reply: Clear permission can make a difference.

asks: A confident answer or one showing its uncertainty?

answers.label: Confident, with a reason
answers.reply: The reason is the useful part.

answers.label: Show the uncertainty
answers.reply: Then we know where to check next.

asks: Repeat an instruction or ask what was understood?

answers.label: Repeat it plainly
answers.reply: Change the words if the first ones failed.

answers.label: Ask what they understood
answers.reply: Then listen for the part you failed to explain.

asks: Talk first or eat while you decide what to say?

answers.label: Talk first
answers.reply: Do not hurry for my benefit.

answers.label: Eat a little
answers.reply: The food is not another question.

asks: What makes an account useful?

answers.label: Another person can check it
answers.reply: Give the place and the time.

answers.label: It says what is missing
answers.reply: And distinguishes missing from deliberately hidden.

asks: Check the first stroke or the closing one?

answers.label: The first stroke
answers.reply: A beginning with a reason! Now follow what it started.

answers.label: The closing stroke
answers.reply: A fine place to stop a very enthusiastic error.

asks: A story with the lesson first or at the end?

answers.label: Lesson first
answers.reply: Good! You can interrupt when the story wanders away from it.

answers.label: At the end
answers.reply: A patient listener! Keep a finger on the point so I can find it again.

asks: Copy a seal neatly or explain each line?

answers.label: Copy it neatly
answers.reply: Then we test whether the neatness belongs to understanding.

answers.label: Explain each line
answers.reply: Excellent! Stop where the explanation becomes a guess.

asks: Will you interrupt when my explanation grows unclear?

answers.label: I will ask straight away
answers.reply: A welcome interruption! Bring two if you need them.

answers.label: I will mark the confusing part
answers.reply: Then show the mark before I move to the next page.

asks: An old note has a different method. Test it or keep today's form?

answers.label: Test it carefully
answers.reply: On spare paper, with no chakra until we understand it.

answers.label: Keep today's form
answers.reply: A sound beginning. Save the question beside it.

asks: What belongs on a new sheet first?

answers.label: The purpose
answers.reply: Splendid! The drawing should know its job.

answers.label: A simple working shape
answers.reply: Then leave room to write what it was for.

asks: Teach a lesson you just learned or practise it again?

answers.label: Teach a small part
answers.reply: Ask the listener what you left unclear.

answers.label: Practise it again
answers.reply: Make one change you can explain afterwards.

asks: Can a question be better than its answer?

answers.label: It can open another path
answers.reply: Then write the path down before I tell another story.

answers.label: An answer still matters
answers.reply: Of course! The path should lead somewhere a person can stand.

asks: Clear handwriting or a beautifully balanced page?

answers.label: Clear handwriting
answers.reply: A gift to the person who must read it in poor light.

answers.label: A balanced page
answers.reply: Keep the working lines clear enough to find under the beauty.

asks: Who makes the last check: the maker or a second reader?

answers.label: The maker again
answers.reply: Fresh eyes after a pause, then.

answers.label: A second reader
answers.reply: And let them tell you where they became uncertain.

asks: A familiar opening or a new problem?

answers.label: The familiar one
answers.reply: Then I can measure what changed in your reply.

answers.label: A new problem
answers.reply: Good. I have three. We will start with the shortest.

asks: Write the list or remember it?

answers.label: Write it down
answers.reply: One less task for a busy head.

answers.label: Remember the essentials
answers.reply: Tell me which ones you cannot afford to lose.

asks: Move first or watch the opening?

answers.label: Move first
answers.reply: Then your opening needs a purpose.

answers.label: Watch the opening
answers.reply: Do not wait so long that waiting becomes the whole plan.

asks: One detailed plan or two simple ones?

answers.label: One detailed plan
answers.reply: Mark where it stops being reliable.

answers.label: Two simple ones
answers.reply: Name what would make us switch.

asks: Record the mistake or the move that fixed it?

answers.label: The mistake
answers.reply: Include what you expected to happen.

answers.label: The correction
answers.reply: Include why it worked, not just where the piece went.

asks: Think with a timer or without one?

answers.label: Use a timer
answers.reply: We can see where the time is actually going.

answers.label: No timer today
answers.reply: Then we finish one position properly.

asks: A map ends. Stop or sketch the next stretch?

answers.label: Stop and check
answers.reply: A sensible use of an unknown edge.

answers.label: Sketch carefully
answers.reply: Mark that it is a sketch, not a promise.

asks: A surprising move: ask why or look for its consequence?

answers.label: Ask why
answers.reply: After I have made one prediction of my own.

answers.label: Look for the consequence
answers.reply: Then compare it with what the player intended.

asks: Who gets to question a plan?

answers.label: Everybody using it
answers.reply: One at a time, with the part that worries them.

answers.label: The person who sees a risk
answers.reply: They must be able to speak before the risk becomes a fact.

asks: Leave a blank line in the plan?

answers.label: For new information
answers.reply: Label the gap so nobody mistakes it for forgetting.

answers.label: No, add a second page
answers.reply: Keep the second page where we can actually find it.

asks: Taste the broth now or wait for it to settle?

answers.label: Taste now
answers.reply: A small spoon. Then we know what the next ingredient changes.

answers.label: Let it settle
answers.reply: Good. Some flavours need room to meet.

asks: Would you rather chop or stir?

answers.label: Chop
answers.reply: I will show how I keep the pieces the same size.

answers.label: Stir
answers.reply: Slowly at the bottom too. That bit gets forgotten.

asks: A big serving or a small one with more waiting?

answers.label: A big serving
answers.reply: Tell me when it is enough. I can still learn that.

answers.label: A small first serving
answers.reply: There is more in the pot. You will not have to ask twice.

asks: Keep a family recipe exact or change one thing?

answers.label: Keep it exact
answers.reply: Then we can taste what they meant to make.

answers.label: Change a little
answers.reply: Write the change down. I always think I will remember.

asks: Save leftovers or invite one more person?

answers.label: Save them properly
answers.reply: Tomorrow deserves something warm too.

answers.label: Invite someone
answers.reply: I know somebody who tends to say they already ate.

asks: Choose your seat or wait to see where there is room?

answers.label: Choose a seat
answers.reply: Leave one beside it if you want company.

answers.label: See where I fit
answers.reply: I can make a little room before everybody sits.

asks: Try the unfamiliar dish or stay with a favourite?

answers.label: Try something new
answers.reply: One taste is enough to begin.

answers.label: Stay with a favourite
answers.reply: That is a good thing to know when I cook for you.

asks: Tell the cook what worked or simply finish the bowl?

answers.label: Name the good part
answers.reply: I like knowing which flavour you noticed.

answers.label: Finish the bowl
answers.reply: That is a clear answer too.

asks: A slightly burnt edge: trim it or start over?

answers.label: Trim the edge
answers.reply: Let us check the middle before giving up the whole thing.

answers.label: Start again
answers.reply: We have time, if the pot is cool enough.

asks: Would you like me to remember your order?

answers.label: Yes, that feels nice
answers.reply: I will leave room for the days you change your mind.

answers.label: Ask each time
answers.reply: Then I can hear what sort of day it has been.

asks: A flower for its colour or its meaning?

answers.label: Its colour
answers.reply: Then say so. Meanings are not instructions.

answers.label: Its meaning
answers.reply: Check whether the receiver knows the same one.

asks: Would you rather I ask about a mood or leave it alone?

answers.label: Ask quietly
answers.reply: You can decline. That is an answer.

answers.label: Leave it alone
answers.reply: I will not make the silence a question.

asks: A hand signal or a spoken warning?

answers.label: Hand signal
answers.reply: Check the other person can see it.

answers.label: Spoken warning
answers.reply: Make the important word first.

asks: Trust a first impression or check another detail?

answers.label: Check another detail
answers.reply: A useful habit. Choose one that could change your mind.

answers.label: Keep the first in mind
answers.reply: Keep it separate from what you actually know.

asks: Give flowers openly or leave them with a note?

answers.label: Give them openly
answers.reply: Then the receiver can ask what you meant.

answers.label: Leave a note
answers.reply: Sign it if you want the meaning to arrive intact.

asks: If I misunderstand you, correct me or wait?

answers.label: I will correct you
answers.reply: Good. I would rather update the reading.

answers.label: Give you a moment
answers.reply: I may still need the correction after the moment.

asks: Bright flowers or ones that open slowly?

answers.label: Bright ones
answers.reply: Easy to find across a room.

answers.label: Slow-opening ones
answers.reply: Then the gift changes after it arrives.

asks: Say what you noticed or ask a question first?

answers.label: Say what I noticed
answers.reply: Keep the observation separate from the explanation.

answers.label: Ask first
answers.reply: Then leave room for an unexpected answer.

asks: A reminder someone came home or a reason they left?

answers.label: Tell me they came home
answers.reply: A clear fact. It can carry enough.

answers.label: Ask why they left
answers.reply: Ask the person, not the empty chair.

asks: Can you be kind without being certain?

answers.label: Yes, begin small
answers.reply: A cup of water does not need a complete theory.

answers.label: Ask what would help
answers.reply: Then listen without replacing the answer.

asks: A precise meeting time or a short window?

answers.label: A precise time
answers.reply: I will make the route allow for arriving calmly.

answers.label: A little window
answers.reply: Then I shall state when the window ends.

asks: A perfect stroke or one that feels like your hand?

answers.label: Perfect form
answers.reply: I can explain the standard if you wish.

answers.label: My own hand
answers.reply: I would like to understand how to practise that.

asks: A rule feels unfair. Ask privately or raise it openly?

answers.label: Ask privately first
answers.reply: A clear question may spare a public misunderstanding.

answers.label: Raise it openly
answers.reply: Then others affected may answer as well.

asks: Titles at practice or simply our given names?

answers.label: Use titles
answers.reply: Then I will make sure I have yours correct.

answers.label: Given names
answers.reply: I shall try. You may remind me if habit wins.

asks: A turn ends early. Offer the next person time or finish another task?

answers.label: Offer the time
answers.reply: I will make clear that accepting it is optional.

answers.label: Finish a small task
answers.reply: Then leave the next person's place ready.

asks: A short report or a full account?

answers.label: Short, with the key fact
answers.reply: I will keep the fuller notes available.

answers.label: A full account
answers.reply: I shall distinguish what I saw from what I concluded.

asks: Repeat the instruction back or begin the attempt?

answers.label: Repeat it back
answers.reply: A chance for both people to correct a misunderstanding.

answers.label: Begin carefully
answers.reply: Then stop if the first step does not fit.

asks: Equal time or time according to need?

answers.label: Equal time
answers.reply: A clear starting rule.

answers.label: More where it is needed
answers.reply: Then the reason should be explained without embarrassing the person.

asks: An exact invitation or one with room to choose?

answers.label: Exact time and place
answers.reply: I can make the path clear.

answers.label: Offer two choices
answers.reply: A manageable amount of freedom. Thank you for limiting the list.

asks: Would you tell me when I sound like a written notice?

answers.label: Tell you gently
answers.reply: I would prefer to know before repeating it.

answers.label: Wait until we are alone
answers.reply: That is considerate. I will listen then.

asks: Nose chooses the walk or we choose before leaving?

answers.label: Follow the nose
answers.reply: Adventure by expert opinion!

answers.label: Choose the route
answers.reply: Fine! Expert opinion gets a vote at each turn!

asks: Sprint first or save it for the finish?

answers.label: Sprint first
answers.reply: A magnificent beginning! We still need legs afterwards!

answers.label: Save the sprint
answers.reply: A dramatic ending! I can appreciate dramatic planning!

asks: Greet a dog at once or wait to be noticed?

answers.label: Wait for the dog
answers.reply: Good manners! The expert approves!

answers.label: Ask the handler first
answers.reply: Excellent! Sometimes the nose is working!

asks: One enormous cheer or lots of little ones?

answers.label: One enormous cheer
answers.reply: I have trained for this precise task!

answers.label: Lots of little ones
answers.reply: A sustained campaign! Very professional!

asks: Eating contest: speed or a favourite dish?

answers.label: Speed round
answers.reply: Small portions! I am interested in victory, not a hospital visit!

answers.label: Favourite dish
answers.reply: Then we both get a good reason to lose slowly!

asks: A running partner ahead or beside you?

answers.label: Ahead to chase
answers.reply: A moving target for my enormous determination!

answers.label: Beside me
answers.reply: Then we can hear when the other needs a slower stretch!

asks: A spoken stop or a raised hand for rest?

answers.label: Say stop
answers.reply: Loud enough for the person making all the noise! That may be me!

answers.label: Raise a hand
answers.reply: Then I promise to look up from my heroic effort!

asks: Wash paws outside or carry the dog to the bath?

answers.label: Wash outside
answers.reply: A sound plan that does not involve lifting an entire opinion!

answers.label: Carry if I can
answers.reply: Ask the dog first! Some passengers are very wiggly!

asks: Lose a game: rematch now or practise tomorrow?

answers.label: Rematch now
answers.reply: Yes! With one useful correction, so it is not just the same noise!

answers.label: Practise tomorrow
answers.reply: Fine! I can become more formidable before breakfast!

asks: Should a loud person notice quiet help?

answers.label: Say thanks clearly
answers.reply: A good use for a voice that carries!

answers.label: Help back quietly
answers.reply: A surprise act of useful competence! I like it!

asks: A herb label: use or warning first?

answers.label: Warning first
answers.reply: Good. The helpful part can wait until the safe part is clear.

answers.label: Use first, then warning
answers.reply: I would still put the warning where the hand reaches.

asks: Learn by drawing the leaf or looking beside a real sample?

answers.label: Draw it carefully
answers.reply: Mark the detail that tells it apart.

answers.label: Use a real sample
answers.reply: Look before touching. I will show the safe part.

asks: Should I ask where it hurts before offering help?

answers.label: Ask first
answers.reply: Then I can avoid making a small pain larger.

answers.label: Tell me what you will do
answers.reply: I can explain before moving anything.

asks: A tidy herb bed or room for plants to spread?

answers.label: Tidy labels and rows
answers.reply: The right leaf is easier to find in a hurry.

answers.label: A little spreading room
answers.reply: Then we need a clear boundary for the ones that should not mix.

asks: Measure again or trust a familiar amount?

answers.label: Measure again
answers.reply: A short check is kinder than a confident error.

answers.label: Check what changed
answers.reply: Yes. A different leaf may need a different amount.

asks: A careful slow attempt or several small ones?

answers.label: One slow attempt
answers.reply: I can watch the whole shape with you.

answers.label: Several small attempts
answers.reply: We will stop between them to note what changed.

asks: A medical word: learn the name or what it means?

answers.label: Learn the name too
answers.reply: I will write it beside the plain explanation.

answers.label: The meaning first
answers.reply: That is the part your hands need to know.

asks: Somebody is tired. Bring water or ask about rest?

answers.label: Bring water
answers.reply: Leave it where they can reach without getting up.

answers.label: Ask about rest
answers.reply: Offer to take one task so resting is possible.

asks: Two plants look alike. Ask or leave them alone?

answers.label: Ask someone trained
answers.reply: Bring the description. Do not taste the evidence.

answers.label: Leave them growing
answers.reply: A safe decision. We can return with the book.

asks: Would you rather hear the uncertainty or a comforting guess?

answers.label: Tell the uncertainty
answers.reply: I can say what we do know as well.

answers.label: Comfort without guessing
answers.reply: That is possible. I can stay without promising what I have not checked.

asks: A staff drill for distance or for control?

answers.label: Distance
answers.reply: Then mind the far end! It arrives before my explanation!

answers.label: Control
answers.reply: A smaller swing! A larger achievement than it sounds!

asks: Test a lantern frame before decorating?

answers.label: Test it first
answers.reply: Grandma would approve before pretending not to!

answers.label: Decorate a little first
answers.reply: Keep the working parts clear! A beautiful collapse is still a collapse!

asks: Say a big ambition aloud or work towards it quietly?

answers.label: Say it aloud
answers.reply: Then people can hold you to the work behind it!

answers.label: Let the work speak
answers.reply: A quieter announcement! I can learn from that!

asks: A new pupil arrives. Introduce everybody or show one friendly face?

answers.label: Introduce the group
answers.reply: Slowly enough that the names have somewhere to land!

answers.label: One friendly face
answers.reply: A good beginning! The rest of us can wait our turn!

asks: Laugh at your own mistake or correct it silently?

answers.label: Laugh, then fix it
answers.reply: That order works! The fixing still has to happen!

answers.label: Fix it quietly
answers.reply: A solid plan! I will try to leave enough quiet for it!

asks: A lantern message: one name or one wish?

answers.label: A name
answers.reply: Somebody you want kept in view!

answers.label: A wish
answers.reply: Then choose one you can help carry tomorrow!

asks: A short speech or time for other people to speak?

answers.label: A short speech
answers.reply: A challenge to my strongest natural technique!

answers.label: Hear the others
answers.reply: Then I should stop preparing my next sentence while they talk!

asks: A future leader: learn names or learn rules first?

answers.label: Learn the names
answers.reply: Then the rules have actual people to answer to!

answers.label: Understand the rules
answers.reply: And ask the people which ones help them!

asks: Win alone or improve beside a strong partner?

answers.label: Win the hard match
answers.reply: Then tell the partner which part made it hard!

answers.label: Improve together
answers.reply: A village-sized answer! I approve at full volume!

asks: A custom: repeat the words or ask what they mean?

answers.label: Repeat them carefully
answers.reply: Then somebody should answer the question after the walk!

answers.label: Ask what they mean
answers.reply: Good! I have questions too, enough for the whole lantern path!

asks: Quiet step or quick step?

answers.label: Quiet
answers.reply: Set the heel later.

answers.label: Quick
answers.reply: Keep the balance.

asks: Point or whisper?

answers.label: Point
answers.reply: Make sure I can see.

answers.label: Whisper
answers.reply: One clear word.

asks: Trim the wick now or before lighting?

answers.label: Now
answers.reply: Good light starts early.

answers.label: Before lighting
answers.reply: Leave time to check.

asks: Known route or new turn?

answers.label: Known route
answers.reply: Check it anyway.

answers.label: New turn
answers.reply: Mark the way back.

asks: Walk beside me or a little behind?

answers.label: Beside
answers.reply: Enough room here.

answers.label: Behind
answers.reply: Watch the other side.

asks: Quiet work: tell someone or leave it done?

answers.label: Tell who needs to know
answers.reply: Briefly.

answers.label: Leave it finished
answers.reply: Check they notice the change.

asks: Under the eave or through the rain?

answers.label: Under the eave
answers.reply: Keep the doorway clear.

answers.label: Through the rain
answers.reply: Wrap the paper first.

asks: A short message or a clear sign?

answers.label: A short message
answers.reply: Write the time.

answers.label: A clear sign
answers.reply: Agree the meaning first.

asks: Wait in sight or out of the way?

answers.label: In sight
answers.reply: Do not block the path.

answers.label: Out of the way
answers.reply: Leave a mark.

asks: For quiet help: words or another useful task?

answers.label: A few words
answers.reply: Enough.

answers.label: Do another task
answers.reply: Ask which one.

asks: Sharpen the tool now or practise with the spare?

answers.label: Sharpen it now
answers.reply: Keep the angle steady.

answers.label: Use the spare
answers.reply: Learn its balance first.

asks: Spend on food or save for better equipment?

answers.label: Food for today
answers.reply: Training needs a body that can finish it.

answers.label: Save for equipment
answers.reply: Know when the saving stops.

asks: One rested hour or two tired ones?

answers.label: One rested hour
answers.reply: Make it work.

answers.label: Two careful hours
answers.reply: Stop before the tired form becomes the normal one.

asks: A cheap repair or wait for a lasting one?

answers.label: A safe cheap repair
answers.reply: Check the part taking the weight.

answers.label: Wait for a lasting one
answers.reply: Borrow safely until then.

asks: Pay for a lesson or learn beside a partner?

answers.label: Pay a good teacher
answers.reply: Ask what the lesson contains.

answers.label: Work with a partner
answers.reply: Bring something useful to their practice.

asks: A harder target or a cleaner first movement?

answers.label: Harder target
answers.reply: Do not let it excuse bad form.

answers.label: Clean first movement
answers.reply: Then keep it when the target changes.

asks: Replace a worn strap or shorten the load?

answers.label: Replace the strap
answers.reply: Check the buckle too.

answers.label: Lighten the load
answers.reply: Say what you left behind.

asks: A free afternoon: rest or paid work?

answers.label: Rest some of it
answers.reply: Enough to return useful.

answers.label: Take the work
answers.reply: Count the time it takes from training.

asks: Explain the effort or show the technique?

answers.label: Explain the useful part
answers.reply: Not the speech about how hard it was.

answers.label: Show the technique
answers.reply: Then repeat it cleanly.

asks: Repay a favour with money or time?

answers.label: Money if useful
answers.reply: Ask what the work was worth.

answers.label: Time at a clear task
answers.reply: Name the day.

asks: Um. The same roof looks different at dawn. Do you like that?

answers.label: I like how it changes
answers.reply: Me too. It is not finished being one thing.

answers.label: I like recognising it
answers.reply: I can keep the shape, even when the colour changes.

asks: Clean paper, or a page somebody already tried on?

answers.label: Clean paper
answers.reply: It is a little frightening. Also nice.

answers.label: A used page
answers.reply: There is less to be afraid of ruining.

asks: Would you rather watch me work, or do something beside me?

answers.label: Watch
answers.reply: All right. Tell me if I start holding my breath.

answers.label: Work beside you
answers.reply: I would like that. We do not have to make the same thing.

asks: What colour does a quiet afternoon feel like?

answers.label: A soft green
answers.reply: Like shade with light still in it. I can see that.

answers.label: A pale grey
answers.reply: Grey has warm bits too. If you look long enough.

asks: Would you keep something you made but never finished?

answers.label: Yes, it is still mine
answers.reply: I have a whole drawer that agrees with you.

answers.label: I would start fresh
answers.reply: Then the first one taught you where to begin.

asks: Is it easier to show one person, or a whole room?

answers.label: One person
answers.reply: I can see one face. That helps.

answers.label: A room
answers.reply: Maybe then I would not have to choose where to look.

asks: A line goes somewhere I did not mean. Erase it or follow it?

answers.label: Follow it
answers.reply: Just for a little while. It could find something.

answers.label: Erase it
answers.reply: I can try the shape again without hurrying.

asks: Um. Is a specific compliment better than just saying something is good?

answers.label: Tell me the small part
answers.reply: The corner, or the light. Something I know you saw.

answers.label: Say how it made you feel
answers.reply: That would tell me something the lines cannot.

asks: If I made you something, should it be useful or just yours?

answers.label: Something useful
answers.reply: Then you could keep it near without needing a reason.

answers.label: Just mine
answers.reply: Oh. That is a reason too.

asks: Does taking a long time mean I care, or that I am afraid to finish?

answers.label: It can mean you care
answers.reply: I like that version. I will still try to finish.

answers.label: Sometimes it is fear
answers.reply: Yes. I think I know when it is that.

asks: Last rice ball. Split it, or race for it?

answers.label: Split it
answers.reply: Fine! I get the bigger half. Kidding. Mostly.

answers.label: Race for it
answers.reply: All right! Nobody tells the pup which way we are running.

asks: Can the pup judge a race if I am in it?

answers.label: Of course
answers.reply: Good judge! Very serious face. Ignore the wagging.

answers.label: Only with another judge
answers.reply: Fine. A committee. The pup wants snacks for the meeting.

asks: Muddy shortcut or the long dry path?

answers.label: Muddy shortcut
answers.reply: Fast route! Shoes off before Grandma sees the mat.

answers.label: Long dry path
answers.reply: We can still race part of it. The dry part, naturally.

asks: Loud cheering, or would that put you off?

answers.label: Make some noise
answers.reply: I have been preparing for this responsibility all my life.

answers.label: Quiet until I finish
answers.reply: Got it. I will put the cheering in my elbows.

asks: Found a tool on the path. Notice board or look for its owner?

answers.label: Put up a notice
answers.reply: I will draw it badly enough that only the owner can recognise it.

answers.label: Look together
answers.reply: Yes! A mission with a very small mystery.

asks: Is it all right if I give you a nickname?

answers.label: If I can give you one
answers.reply: Deal! Make it something fast.

answers.label: Ask me before using it
answers.reply: All right. It is yours, so you get a vote.

asks: Pick the next race: fewer jumps or a trickier landing?

answers.label: Fewer jumps, faster run
answers.reply: Speed round! No hiding behind a fancy hop.

answers.label: Trickier landing
answers.reply: We check the landing first. I do listen in class sometimes.

asks: If I am late, do you come looking or wait where we agreed?

answers.label: Come looking
answers.reply: Start at the food stalls. That is a useful clue.

answers.label: Wait where we agreed
answers.reply: Then I know where to run back to. That helps.

asks: One person gets the praise. Should they name everybody who helped?

answers.label: Name everybody
answers.reply: Exactly! Someone held the ladder. That matters.

answers.label: Let them have the moment
answers.reply: Fair. We can tell the others afterwards.

asks: Does a tiny bit of help still count when nobody notices?

answers.label: It still counts
answers.reply: Good. I was hoping the small stuff had somewhere to go.

answers.label: Tell somebody it helped
answers.reply: Then I will say it. You waiting helped.
